reviewers.summary: The analysis is unacceptably incomplete for any research claim: it confuses association with causation in the title, reports a p-value rounded to zero (0.0000), omits the confidence interval for the mean difference, lacks any covariate adjustment despite an observational design, and is not bound to a pre-specified analysis plan. These issues make the result uninterpretable for publication or external sharing.

findings.title: Unadjusted comparison in observational data with causal phrasing
findings.whyItMatters: The title asks 'Does the continuous outcome differ by treatment group' which implies a causal question, but the analysis is an unadjusted Welch t-test on observational data with no confounding control. This cannot answer whether the outcome differs *because* of treatment; only an association is estimable. The difference may be entirely due to selection bias or confounding.
findings.actionableFix: Reframe the question as an association and either adjust for confounders using a multivariable model or explicitly state that no causal conclusion is intended and discuss confounding as a major limitation. If causal intent, redesign with a target trial framework and confounder control.
findings.deterministicVerification: Verify that the analysis plan includes confounding control or acknowledges the absence of it. Check that title and abstract reflect associational language.

findings.title: P-value rounded to zero and reported as 'p=0.0000'
findings.whyItMatters: The exact p-value is 3.83e-10, which should be reported as p<0.001 (or p=3.8×10^{-10}). Writing p=0.0000 is a rounding error that suggests a zero probability, which is scientifically and statistically incorrect. It misleads readers about the strength of evidence and is contrary to standard reporting guidelines.
findings.actionableFix: Report p-value using scientific notation (e.g., p=3.8×10^{-10}) or, if less precise, p<0.001. Never round a p-value to zero.
findings.deterministicVerification: Confirm that the printed p-value in the manuscript matches the stats-run output (3.8287252527457425e-10) and that the rounded version is not zero.

findings.title: Missing confidence interval for the mean difference
findings.whyItMatters: A p-value alone does not convey the precision of the estimate. The manuscript reports only the mean difference (2.9137) and p-value, but no 95% CI. The reader cannot assess the practical significance or the range of effect sizes compatible with the data.
findings.actionableFix: Calculate and report a 95% Welch confidence interval for the difference in means. Include it in the abstract and results.
findings.deterministicVerification: The CI can be derived from the means, standard deviations, and sample sizes; re-run the t-test to obtain the interval and confirm it appears in the manuscript.

findings.title: No pre-specified analysis plan (unbound run)
findings.whyItMatters: The result posture is 'exploratory_standard_table' and cannot support method-governed inference. Presenting this as a confirmatory 'does differ' question risks p-hacking and overinterpretation. Without a pre-registered analysis, the p-value has no confirmatory meaning.
findings.actionableFix: Either relegate the analysis to a purely exploratory stage and remove inferential language, or create a formal analysis specification that pre-defines the comparison, outcomes, handling of missing data, and sensitivity checks, then re-run under binding.
findings.deterministicVerification: Check that the stats-run binding.status field is 'bound' and references a valid spec; verify that the manuscript states the binding.

findings.title: Assumption verification incomplete (normality, outliers)
findings.whyItMatters: Although the Welch t-test is robust to moderate non-normality with these sample sizes, no formal check of normality or outlier inspection is documented. Levene's test alone is insufficient. Garbage in, garbage out: if the data are contaminated with outliers or a heavy-tailed distribution, the p-value and effect size may be misleading.
findings.actionableFix: Provide summary statistics (per-group mean, SD, median, IQR), a boxplot (already generated but not discussed), and a normality diagnostic (e.g., Shapiro-Wilk for each group or Q-Q plots). Address extreme values.
findings.deterministicVerification: Confirm the figures/diagnostics artifact includes distribution plots and that the manuscript comments on them.

findings.title: Cohort flow and missingness not described
findings.whyItMatters: The manuscript claims 240 complete cases but does not state the initial sample size, number excluded, or reasons. Without this, selection bias cannot be assessed. If missing data are non-random, the results could be biased.
findings.actionableFix: Provide a STROBE-like flow diagram showing eligibility criteria, exclusions, and missingness. If no missing data, state that all records had complete outcome and treatment variables.
findings.deterministicVerification: Check that the counts reconcile with the raw data: sum of excluded + complete-case equals starting N.

findings.title: Data availability and provenance not declared
findings.whyItMatters: The manuscript references 'local research dataset' and includes artifact hashes, but does not state whether the data itself is available, what restrictions apply, or how a reader could obtain it. For a local analysis this may be acceptable, but a data availability statement is expected.
findings.actionableFix: Add a Data Availability section that clarifies that the dataset is not publicly shared (e.g., due to institutional policy) and describes how methodological materials can be accessed.
findings.deterministicVerification: No raw data file is present in the run directory; confirm that the statement matches the actual access policy.

findings.title: Extremely small p-value warrants sensitivity check
findings.whyItMatters: A p-value of 3.8e-10 with only 240 observations and a moderate Cohen's d (0.87) is unusual and could indicate mis-specified standard errors, data entry error, or a degenerate distribution. Without inspecting the raw data, this result is not credible enough to publish.
findings.actionableFix: Verify the data: compute per-group standard deviations, check for constant outcomes or near-constant clusters. If the data are grouped in a way that violates independence, use alternative methods. Report per-group SD in the manuscript.
findings.deterministicVerification: The t-statistic is (mean_diff) / (pooled SE). From given n's and d, we can back-calculate: pooled SD = mean_diff / (d * sqrt((1/n_a + 1/n_b)))? Actually standard formula: d = (mean_a - mean_b) / Spooled, where Spooled = sqrt(((n_a-1)*var_a + (n_b-1)*var_b)/(n_a+n_b-2)). With d=0.874, mean_diff=2.914, so Spooled = 2.914/0.874 = 3.335. Then SE = Spooled * sqrt(1/n_a + 1/n_b) = 3.335 * sqrt(1/96+1/144) = 3.335*0.130 = 0.433. t = 2.914/0.433 = 6.73 (close to 6.59). p from t=6.59 with df approx 178 (Welch) is indeed extremely small. Check raw SDs from data to ensure they are not artificially low.

missingEvidence: Raw data or per-group summary statistics (SD, min, max, median, IQR)
Cohort construction details (inclusion/exclusion flow, missing data patterns)
Confidence interval for the mean difference

reviewers.summary: This manuscript reports an unbound exploratory Welch's t-test as if it were a confirmatory study. The analysis lacks pre-specification, cohort definitions, variable documentation, literature context, and contains reporting errors. Without these, it is not suitable for publication or claim. Major revisions are needed, including binding the analysis to a protocol and providing full data provenance.

findings.title: Exploratory analysis presented as confirmatory test
findings.whyItMatters: The analysis is unbound (exploratory_standard_table) and lacks a pre-specified analysis plan. P-values and effect sizes from such an analysis are not reliable for inference and cannot support paper-ready conclusions.
findings.actionableFix: Clearly label the analysis as exploratory and remove definitive p-value language, or bind the run to a pre-registered analysis spec and re-run under governance before making any confirmatory claims.

findings.title: P-value reported as 0.0000 instead of exact or <0.001 notation
findings.whyItMatters: Reporting p=0.0000 erroneously implies a probability of zero and obscures the true extreme value (3.83e-10). This misleads readers about the strength of evidence.
findings.actionableFix: Report the exact p-value (e.g., 3.83×10⁻¹⁰) or use standard notation such as p<0.001. Never round to zero.

findings.title: Missing cohort eligibility criteria and variable definitions
findings.whyItMatters: Without inclusion/exclusion rules, definition of treatment groups, and outcome measurement details, the study cannot be reproduced or externally validated.
findings.actionableFix: Add a detailed cohort construction section, including data source, eligibility rules, missingness handling, and a data dictionary defining all variables (units, coding).

findings.title: No literature review or clinical context provided
findings.whyItMatters: The study lacks any reference to prior work, clinical relevance, or the research gap it addresses. This prevents readers from assessing the importance and novelty of the findings.
findings.actionableFix: Include a brief literature review and explicitly state the research question in the context of existing evidence.

findings.title: Manuscript contains self-contradictory placeholder text
findings.whyItMatters: The Limitations section states 'No reader-facing paper/manuscript artifact was found.' while the manuscript itself exists. This indicates incomplete editing and generic template remnants, undermining credibility.
findings.actionableFix: Remove all boilerplate and irrelevant statements; tailor every statement to the actual analysis and artifacts present.

findings.title: No normality or distributional check reported
findings.whyItMatters: Although Welch’s t-test is robust with large samples, reporting diagnostic checks (e.g., normality, outliers) increases transparency and helps readers assess assumptions.
findings.actionableFix: Include a histogram, Q-Q plot, and Shapiro-Wilk test per group, with appropriate caveats if violations are found.

findings.title: No information on data provenance or outcome plausibility
findings.whyItMatters: Without knowing what 'outcome_cont' represents, its measurement units, or how data were collected, the mean difference of 2.91 is uninterpretable and data quality cannot be assessed.
findings.actionableFix: Provide a clear description of the data source, collection methods, outcome definition, units, and any data cleaning steps.

findings.title: Abstract and results omit group sizes and imbalance
findings.whyItMatters: The unequal group sizes (96 vs. 144) may affect generalizability and interpretation of effect size. Readers need this information to assess the study.
findings.actionableFix: Report n for each group in the abstract and results section, including any comment on imbalance if relevant.

missingEvidence: Pre-registered analysis protocol or AnalysisSpec artifact
Raw data or data dictionary with variable definitions and units
Cohort eligibility criteria and missing data handling report
Documentation of data source and ethical approvals

reviewPanel.nextAction: Adjudicate findings and route accepted repairs back into the pipeline.
